facts.t: The 17th Lok Sabha never had a Deputy Speaker
facts.d: Article 93 says the House shall choose one as soon as may be — with no deadline attached. The post stayed vacant for the entire term, the first time in independent India, and remained unfilled into the 18th.

facts.t: A Speaker once defied his own party and was expelled for it
facts.d: Somnath Chatterjee refused the CPI(M)'s direction to withdraw support during the 2008 nuclear-deal confidence vote, on the ground that the Speaker belongs to the House rather than to a party. The party expelled him.

facts.t: Britain's Speaker resigns from the party and contests as an independent
facts.d: On election, a Commons Speaker severs all party ties and stands for re-election as Speaker seeking re-election. India has no such convention — which is why the Halim Committee and the 170th Law Commission both recommended importing it.

bank.q: Under Article 94(c) a Speaker may be removed by a resolution passed by:
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
A majority of all the then members of the House
A two-thirds majority of members present and voting
A special majority of both Houses
bank.e: An absolute majority of the total membership — which is why a Speaker backed by the ruling majority is nearly irremovable.

bank.q: With reference to the removal of a Speaker, consider the following statements:
s: The Speaker cannot preside while the resolution is being considered.
The Speaker may speak and vote in the first instance but has no casting vote.
bank.e: All three are correct, arising from the proviso to Article 94 and from Articles 96(1) and 96(2).

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT an exclusive function of the Lok Sabha Speaker?
o: Exercising a casting vote on equality of votes
Serving as ex-officio President of the Indian Parliamentary Group
bank.e: The casting vote under Article 100 belongs to all presiding officers, not to the Speaker alone.

bank.q: Match List I (country) with List II (practice on presiding officers):
pairs: 2. Speaker severs party ties and contests as an independent
3. Written codes of conduct with decisions subject to review
4. The Speaker's rulings are open to discussion
bank.e: Britain's independent Speaker, Australia's discussable rulings, Canada's rotating deputies, and New Zealand's written codes.

bank.as: Nabam Rebia held that a Speaker facing a removal notice should not decide disqualification petitions.
bank.rs: The rule is itself open to tactical abuse by members facing disqualification.
bank.e: Both statements are true, but the Reason is a criticism of the rule rather than an explanation of why it was laid down. The rationale was the conflict of interest inherent in a Speaker adjudicating while his own tenure is in question.

s: N. Sanjiva Reddy resigned from his party in 1969 while contesting for President.
Somnath Chatterjee ignored a party direction during the 14th Lok Sabha.
Sumitra Mahajan's certification of Aadhaar as a Money Bill remains contentious.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they map the whole spectrum from principled neutrality to contested partisanship.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed reforms for the office of Speaker EXCEPT:
o: Mandatory resignation from the party on the British model
A three-month deadline for anti-defection rulings
Making the Speaker's rulings entirely immune from judicial review
bank.e: Limited judicial review is listed among the problems. Raja Ram Pal already permits review for substantive illegality despite Article 122.

bank.q: The Deputy Speaker's appointment under Article 93 is governed by:
o: No timeline — the article says only as soon as may be
A ninety-day timeline set by the Rules
bank.e: No timeline exists, which is how the post stayed vacant for an entire Lok Sabha. A sixty-day limit is among the proposed reforms.

bank.q: With reference to the office of Vice-President, consider the following:
s: Its normal function is legislative and its contingent function executive.
The electoral college includes members of state legislative assemblies.
The Rajya Sabha never dissolves, giving its Chairman continuity.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. States do not vote in the Vice-Presidential election even though the office chairs the Council of States — a standing criticism.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a weakness of the Vice-Presidency?
o: A partisan election for an impartial office
Lok Sabha predominance in the electoral college
Election by both Houses conferring bicameral legitimacy
Article 68's lack of an outer limit for filling a casual vacancy
bank.e: Bicameral legitimacy is listed among the strengths of the office, not its weaknesses.

bank.q: The 2026 motion against Speaker Om Birla was, constitutionally speaking:
bank.e: A removal resolution under Article 94(c). It was negatived by voice vote — which is why recorded voting is among the proposed reforms.

bank.q: Consider the following problems with the removal procedure:
s: The requirement of fifty members rising shuts out small parties.
Rule 200A admissibility can operate as a gatekeeping tool.
An independent fact-finding mechanism examines the allegations before the vote.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There is no independent fact-finding at all — a preliminary all-party scrutiny committee is among the proposed remedies.
